newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends at record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends at record closing high.

text.p: * Value turnover heavy at 4.4 billion pesos
The Manila share index finished on Thursday at a record closing high of 3,392.76 points, up by 19.15 points, or 0.57 percent, on a surge in blue chips, traders said.
"It was San Miguel Corp B that started everything and it was followed by other blue chips," said Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities Inc.
In early trade, the index sharply rose breaking out of the 3,400 mark but mild profit-taking in mid-session caused the index to close off its intra-day high of 3,404.80 points.
The market's previous all-time high was 3,375.94 points achieved July last year.
Besides San Miguel, other big cap issues that rose were PLDT, Ayala Land, Petron, and the Philippine National Bank.
The jubilant mood at the exchange, however, was marred by a computer glitch minutes before the end of trading that prevented some brokers from entering orders.
The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) information technology department, however, could not immediately explain the technical problem.
All indices rose except for the banking sector. Gainers outnumbered losers 87 to 51 with 59 issues unchanged.
Traders expect the market to continue its surge on Friday, saying the index will likely vault above the 3,400 level.
"We are not yet in an overbought situation and if ever we will see profit-taking it will be slight," Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president for institutional sales at Philippine Asia Equity, said.
